thread:
Maya: quick thought  add per-tier sample-rate knobs to circuit-breaker telemetry so we don't explode logs when routing across a bunch of model variants for low tiers
Sam: +1. main question: what are the absolute minimal fields we need to retain to debug routing after aggressive sampling? :thinking:
Li: minimum: request_id, route_decision, model_variant, latency_ms, cb_state. Everything else can be sampled.
Nina: and we still need aggregate counters at 100% (decision counts, fallback counts) so we can detect policy thrashing.
Maya: agree. propose a lightweight "route_brief" summary emitted every minute per route with counters so sampling doesn't hide macro behaviour.
Alex: how do we express sample rates in the policy model? per-tier? per-action? per-variant?
Li: per-tier + per-action. fallback telemetry lower samples, primary region higher. also a global max_events cap to protect infra.
Maya: sketch of policy proto (pseudo):
```
policy {
  tier: "standard"
  slo_conditions { metric: "p95_latency_ms" window: "5m" threshold: 200 }
  actions: ["fallback_variant:v-small", "reduce_fanout:1"]
  telemetry { sample_rate: 0.01 route_brief_interval: "60s" }
}
```
Sam: operational concerns: (1) in-flight requests when CB flips -> do graceful completion on old path, new requests follow new decision (add grace_period param). (2) rollout UX in console so customers can preview behavior before enabling.
Nina: graceful_inflight: boolean + grace_period_seconds default 10. we should also expose a "drain_mode" for pods handling old sessions.
Alex: console preview idea: opt-in simulation per route that replays last N minutes of traces and shows expected changes (latency delta, cost delta, fallback_rate). show an audit timeline for policy flips.
Maya: sampling implications for simulation: we need deterministic replay; route_brief + sampled traces should be enough if we lift-sample during simulation.
Sam: quotas note: if a customer gets frequently downgraded, that could be masking insufficient capacity. surface a "fallback_rate" metric per customer and tie alerting thresholds to tier.
ops-bot: [incident-bot] created alert "fallback_rate_enterprise_high" threshold 0.05 over 10m
Nina: alerts by default: enterprise -> page on >5% over 10m; standard -> warn in console; free -> record for billing insights only.
Li: API debate: full JS predicates are powerful but opaque. prefer declarative DSL plus a server-side function escape hatch owned by infra. simulation + static analysis becomes tractable with declarative policies.
Alex: agreed. also add a policy-simulator API endpoint developers can call from console. show estimated RPS impact and token-cost delta.
Maya: action items: Li draft telemetry sampling schema + route_brief proto; Nina write graceful in-flight spec; Alex mock console preview + sim UI; Sam prototype policy-simulator PoC and push link here.
Sam: will try PoC by EOD and attach repo link in thread.
Maya: thanks all  sync in 2 days. tagging @product to keep them looped :wave:
